thread:
maria: seeing a big latency spike across continuous-batcher in us-east-1 — tail latency > 5s and a flood of CUDA OOMs. pages are spiking, lots of paging warnings. root error in logs: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-3417 — continuous-batcher heap surge, affect: hosted API (text/generate) — paging + node flaps. Severity: P1.

aj: i'm the oncall, joining. which customer hit first?

sophie: CS alert — acme-inc and two other mid-market customers reported timeouts ~10:04 UTC. routing shows requests forwarded to batcher nodes that started restarting.

devin: pasting trimmed logs from batcher on node rtx-prod-07:

```
[2026-03-15T10:03:21Z] batcher: kvcache.size=1.2GB prefetch.pending=5342
[2026-03-15T10:03:22Z] serve: batch.size=4096 merging->accumulator
[2026-03-15T10:03:22Z] runtime: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at serve.cc:421
[2026-03-15T10:03:22Z] containerd: process exited code=137 signal=9
[2026-03-15T10:03:23Z] docker: restarting container
```

maria: that batch.size=4096 looks wrong — we've seen runaway accumulator merges before. suspect continuous-batcher growth loop (accumulator not being truncated).

aj: immediate plan: (1) mark node rtx-prod-07 unschedulable and drain, (2) temporarily throttle incoming batcher traffic by toggling runtime flag, (3) disable prefetch on batchers cluster-wide. i'll coordinate.

devin: commands i'm running now:

```
kubectl cordon rtx-prod-07
kubectl drain rtx-prod-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/flags" -d '{"continuous_batching.throttle":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```

ops-incident-bot: @aj set cluster flag continuous_batching.throttle=true (applied to: us-east-1-batcher-pool) — rollout started.

sophie: informing CS+AE for acme-inc: "We've throttled batching and are draining affected nodes; your requests may see reduced throughput but improved stability. will follow up after mitigation."

devin: after throttle and draining the repeated OOMs dropped dramatically. still seeing a handful of restarts from a different node (rtx-prod-02) where kvcache grew to 900MB. suspect leak + prefetch interacting with accumulator growth.

maria: can we toggle kvcache.prefetch=false for batchers in prod? cheap quick hit if it reduces memory pressure.

aj: doing it now.

```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/flags" -d '{"kvcache.prefetch":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```

infra-bot: Flag update acknowledged — kvcache.prefetch=false applied to us-east-1-batcher-pool.

oncall-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-3417 status -> triage in progress. pagers: removed noisy node rtx-prod-07 from rotation.

devin: pushing a short-lived mitigation: limit batch merge window to 200ms and cap accumulator size to 256 entries via runtime env (BATCHER_ACCUM_MAX=256). patch applied via emergency config.

maria: good. observing 95th latency drop from 3.8s -> 420ms after flags and caps. customer timeouts reduced.

aj: handing off to devin for deeper debugging and fixes. i'll stay available. @devin take lead; i'll mark as on-call handoff in incident tracker.

ops-incident-bot: @aj -> @devin incident handoff recorded. next response window assigned.

devin: root cause hypothesis: an edge case in merge logic allowed accumulator to accept very large batches when prefetch interleaves KB requests, causing runaway memory allocation. repr steps: reproduce with synthetic load that mixes long-prefix cache hits + high concurrency.

maria: can you open an emergency PR with the cap + safe-guard plus instrumentation? we need backport to prod-branch.

devin: created PR #12356 (hotfix) with accumulator cap and an extra guard to hard-fail merges that would exceed mem thresholds. CI green; preparing canary rollout. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/inference/pulls/12356

sophie: CS: acme-inc acknowledges the mitigation and wants ETA for permanent fix. replying: "hotfix deployed to canary, will roll to prod in 30m if stable; postmortem and timeline by EOD."

aj: monitoring: rolling canary to 10% nodes now. metrics show no OOMs on canary. planning full rollout in 25m if clean.

infra-bot: canary rollout progress: 10% -> 50% -> 100% on us-east-1-batcher-pool (completed).

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation successful. customer impact reduced to degraded throughput for ~18 minutes during throttles.

devin: follow-ups captured: (a) backport hotfix to 2026-prod-branch, (b) add accumulator size metric + alert if > 200 entries, (c) add automated circuit-breaker to fail fast when paging rate > threshold, (d) run chaos test for prefetch+merge case. created tasks: TASK-987, TASK-988, TASK-989.

maria: also add a playbook step to throttle continuous-batching and disable prefetch as a rapid mitigation; put exact ops-api commands in playbook.

aj: final note for the incident record: total affected customers: 3 paying accounts; severity P1; incident window ~10:03-10:25 UTC. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre for postmortem.

ops-incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3417 RESOLVED (mitigated). Please fill the postmortem template: https://wiki.internal/incidents/INC-2026-3417.

sophie: leaving a short customer-facing summary in the CS ticket and setting expectation for EOD postmortem.

maria: thanks everyone. great rapid coordination. closing thread after postmortem is filed.
